root_motivation: An elderly companion AI fields the same questions repeatedly (e.g. 'what day is it?', 'what did I have for breakfast?'). Each repeat costs a full Sonnet API turn. By caching semantically-equivalent utterances via embedding similarity, the vast majority of repeated questions can be answered for zero API cost — while a hard cache-unsafe gate prevents the cache from ever serving stale time/weather/calendar answers that would be a harmful lie.
user_persona: jsy, running a companion assistant for his mother at home. The assistant runs on a local device. API budget is finite; the same 10-20 questions repeat across the day. A wrong answer about time or calendar is worse than a cache miss.

acceptance_criteria.description: store then lookup of a paraphrase (different words, same meaning) returns the cached response when cosine >= threshold, using a deterministic stubbed embedder (no live socket in tests).
lookup of an unrelated utterance (cosine < threshold) returns None (no false hit), proven with a fixture pair using the stubbed embedder.

Cache-unsafe gate: an utterance classified cache-unsafe returns None from lookup and is rejected by store, even when an identical entry exists — tested by pre-seeding a 'what time is it' entry and asserting it is never served.
TTL expiry: an entry past its ttl_secs is not served. Proven with a frozen/injected clock so no wall-clock flakiness.
Max-entry bound enforced with LRU eviction: exceeding the bound evicts the least-recently-hit entry. Proven by inserting bound+1 entries and asserting the oldest-unused one is gone.
Embedder client is dim-agnostic (works with any f32 vec length). If the embed socket is unreachable, lookup returns None (cache miss) — never panics. Proven with a failing embedder stub.
A deflection metric is exposed: hits_count and total_lookups_count accessible on SemCache, so the caller can compute hit rate.
cargo test green; cargo clippy -D warnings clean; MSRV 1.85, no let-chains.

scope: A Rust library crate (--target lib) providing SemCache: an embedding-keyed response cache
Cosine similarity lookup via dot product on L2-normalized f32 vectors
A pluggable Embedder trait so tests use a deterministic stub; production uses recall's embed RPC
cache-unsafe gate: a per-entry flag and a well-known unsafe-intent set (time, weather, calendar)
TTL-based expiry with injected clock (ClockFn) for deterministic tests
LRU eviction when entry count exceeds a configured capacity bound
Deflection metrics: hits_count + total_lookups_count on SemCache
cargo clippy -D warnings clean at MSRV 1.85, no let-chains
non_goals: Does NOT implement the recall embed RPC client — it accepts any impl Embedder; wiring to recall is the caller's concern
Does NOT classify intents — the cache_safe flag is set by the caller (wm-skills) at store time; wm-semcache does not parse utterances
Does NOT persist cache to disk — in-memory only in v1
Does NOT run a network server or IPC socket — pure library, no async runtime
Does NOT implement cache warming, pre-population, or bulk import
Does NOT handle multi-language or multi-model embedding alignment

additional.note: Library must compile with zero dependencies in the happy path; only thiserror and similar lightweight crates allowed

five_whys_trace.q: Why build an embedding-keyed response cache?
five_whys_trace.a: Because the companion assistant for jsy's mother answers the same questions many times per day, and each repeat is a full Sonnet API call.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does every repeat cost a full API call?
five_whys_trace.a: There is no semantic deduplication layer. Exact-string matching misses paraphrases ('what time is it?' vs 'do you know the time?').

five_whys_trace.q: Why not just use a simple exact-match cache?
five_whys_trace.a: Natural language questions from elderly users are never exactly repeated — small wording variations bypass exact-match but carry identical intent.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is a stale-time-answer worse than a cache miss?
five_whys_trace.a: For an elderly user depending on the assistant for orientation (time, appointments), a confident wrong answer erodes trust and can cause real harm. A cache miss just costs one API call; a stale hit is a confident lie.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should the cache-unsafe classification be learned or hardcoded?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Hardcoded set of unsafe intents for v1 (time, date, weather, calendar-today, reminders-today). The caller passes cache_safe: bool at store time; the library only enforces the contract, not the classification.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What similarity threshold is the default?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: 0.85 cosine similarity as the default, configurable at SemCache construction time. Tests use a deterministic stub so threshold behavior is proven without floating-point flakiness from a real embedder.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should the Embedder trait be async?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Sync for v1. The library has no async runtime dep. Wiring to an async recall client is the caller's responsibility (they can block_on at the call site if needed).
